title: Scenario 2 knowledge check
notes: PROVISIONAL INSTRUMENT. Revised 2026-10-28 so every item tests real farming knowledge that the game and its feedback actually teach, in plain language for smallholder farmers. Still needs supervisor review before any study use. Editing this file is enough to change the instrument - no code changes are required. Pest-outbreak bean season: scout to find the outbreak while it is small, treat before it spreads, keep farming the rest of the field.

questions.text: When scouting a bean field for pests, where should you look?
options: Along the edge of the field, since that is where pests come in
Across the field: under leaves, on new growth and on the pods
At the biggest plants, because pests always go for the strongest
At the soil around the plants, looking for insect holes
questions.explanation: Aphids, whiteflies and pod borers hide under leaves, in soft new growth and on pods, and an outbreak usually starts in one patch. Checking several plants in different parts of the field is how you find it while it is small - which is what the scout tool did this season.

questions.text: You find aphids on a few bean plants in one corner of the field. What is the best first step?
options: Spray the whole field several times to be safe
Leave them - a few aphids never cause real damage
Wait and deal with them after the harvest
Treat those plants now and check the plants around them
questions.explanation: Caught early, an outbreak can be handled on just the affected plants (remove them, wash the insects off, or a targeted treatment), then the neighbouring plants checked over the next few days. Spraying everything costs more and also kills the ladybirds that eat aphids. Left alone, a few aphids become thousands within weeks and spread.

questions.text: Why should the rest of the crop still be watered and cared for while you deal with a pest outbreak?
options: Healthy, well-watered plants cope with pest damage much better
It should not - all effort should go to the pests until they are gone
Watering should stop, because wet plants attract more pests
It makes no difference - pests harm healthy and weak plants equally
questions.explanation: A plant that is short of water and under attack loses condition from both at once and recovers badly. Keeping the rest of the field watered stops pest damage piling on top of drought damage - and the rest of the season's work still has to get done.
